draft.title: Multiplying and dividing integers
card: Integers are whole numbers, positive, negative or zero. To multiply or divide, first look at the signs of the two numbers.
the answer is positive. For example, \(-6 \times (-3) = 18\) and \(-20 \div (-4) = 5\).
the answer is negative. For example, \(7 \times (-2) = -14\) and \(20 \div (-4) = -5\).
Work out the sign first, then multiply or divide the numbers as if they had no signs. Division uses the same sign rules as multiplication.
draft.remember: Same signs give a positive answer. Different signs give a negative answer.

a.why: Both numbers are negative, so the signs are the same and the answer is positive. \(8 \times 5 = 40\). The answer \(-40\) comes from forgetting that two negatives make a positive.
a.clue: Check whether the two signs match.

b.q: A diver off the coast of Portsea, in Victoria, goes down at a steady rate. Her height changes by \(-4\) m each minute. What is her total change in height over 6 minutes?
b.why: Six lots of \(-4\) m is \(6 \times (-4)\). The signs are different, so the answer is negative, and \(6 \times 4 = 24\), so the change is \(-24\) m. The answer 24 m drops the sign, and \(-10\) m adds the numbers instead of multiplying.
b.clue: Each minute adds another \(-4\) m. How many minutes are there?
